title: TASSO: TAsk-Specific Subspace Optimization for Continual Learning of Vision-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.21487v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) exhibit strong zero-shot capabilities, making them an attractive solution for continual learning across diverse tasks. However, during continual adaptation, both catastrophic forgetting and zero-shot degradation occur, severely degrading performance. In this paper, we introduce TASSO, a new paradigm that efficiently preserves the latent space geometry while ensuring network plasticity. We achieve this with two complementary techniques: subspace learning and geometry-aware knowledge distillation. Specifically, we first learn a sequence of task-specific low-rank projectors, which we use to project the latent representations before optimizing cross-entropy. Secondly, we employ a geodesic-distance-based loss that distills knowledge from the previous-task model while effectively preserving the latent space geometry. translated_title: TASSO：面向视觉-语言模型持续学习的任务特定子空间优化
translated_abstract: 视觉-语言模型（VLMs）展现出强大的零样本能力，使其成为跨多样任务持续学习的理想解决方案。然而，在持续适应过程中，会出现灾难性遗忘和零样本性能退化，严重降低模型性能。本文提出TASSO，一种新范式，能够在确保网络可塑性的同时高效保持潜在空间几何结构。我们通过两种互补技术实现这一目标：子空间学习和几何感知知识蒸馏。具体而言，我们首先学习一系列任务特定的低秩投影器，在优化交叉熵之前将潜在表示投影到这些子空间中。其次，我们采用基于测地距离的损失函数，从先前任务模型中蒸馏知识，同时有效保持潜在空间的几何结构。这些设计选择不仅避免了沿全嵌入维度进行不必要的参数更新，还显著提升了持续学习性能。
tldr: TASSO通过任务特定低秩子空间投影和测地距离知识蒸馏，在持续学习视觉-语言模型时同时缓解灾难性遗忘和零样本退化，保持潜在空间几何结构。
en_tdlr: TASSO mitigates catastrophic forgetting and zero-shot degradation in continual learning of vision-language models via task-specific low-rank subspace projection and geodesic-distance-based knowledge distillation, preserving latent space geometry.
